question_text: A 27-year-old Hispanic G2P1 presents for a routine antepartum visit at 26 weeks gestation. She has no complaints. The vital signs are normal, the physical examination is within normal limits, and the gynecologic examination corresponds to 25 weeks gestation. The oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) with a 75-g glucose load is significant for a glucose level of 177 mg/dL at 1 hour and 167 mg/dL at 2 hour. The fasting blood glucose level is 138 mg/dL (7.7 mmol/L), and the HbA1c is 7%. Which of the following represents the proper initial management?
